missionPremise: P-255's live census (2026-09-16T18:15:14.495Z, 981,405 parcels; reproduced in OPS-16 ruling A-185) measured 219,472 six-county parcels carrying `absent-verified` on all five setback rails where NOTHING established an absence: 125,212 district misses and 94,260 no-table-city parcels, 61,725 of the misses being planned-development codes (A-164). The row rests on a vocabulary fact read at source (hauska-factory src/lib/parcel-record-engine/cell-state.js): `absent-verified` is in EARNED_CELL_KINDS and `isPublishable` returns true for it, while `unaccounted` is neither earned nor publishable. So a writer that stamps `absent-verified` because a TABLE is missing is making a publishable claim about a parcel on the strength of a fact about a document -- and the rail gate, which reads earned cells as decided, believed it. The row's own words: 'STOP WRITING CHECKED, NONE REQUIRED WHERE NOTHING WAS CHECKED.'

leave_behind.text: The staging dry run and apply for factory-parcel-setback-cells, six counties, after P-252 is live. Predictions to check against, per county (per parcel, 5 cells each): 48021 refused 1925 / unaccounted 3593; 48055 644 / 4472; 48209 6498 / 12406; 48309 2252 / 41053; 48453 21054 / 82229; 48491 29352 / 13994. A county whose applied numbers differ from these is a finding, not a rounding error -- the difference would be parcels the census's inventory could not see.

An operator ruling on UNZONED / NOT ZONED and the other no-code tokens: if a city's staged layer asserts them as a real attribute of the surface, they belong in the not-applicable set; if the adapter writes them as a fallback for an unreadable code, they belong where they are now (unaccounted). This lane took the honest side rather than guessing. The read that would settle it is parcel-r5-zoning.mjs's and the adapters' write path, not this job's.

A candidate classification and a writer's assertion are different products of the same regex. P-255's census could legitimately report ROW/WATER/UNZONED as CANDIDATES for not-applicable; a writer stamping a cell has to ASSERT, and 'candidate' spelled into a write becomes the very defect the row closes one state over. When one rule has two implementations in two repos, copy the report, split the assert, and record the split as the divergence -- do not let the report's tolerance leak into the write.

A whole-file scan for a forbidden literal is a weaker instrument than it looks: it cannot distinguish prose that must name the removed state from code that emits it, and it cannot see a state assembled at runtime. Assert over the states a code path EMITS (drive the real function over every branch and inspect the output), and enforce the same invariant at the write boundary with a refusal.

Delete a counter you can no longer move rather than leaving it at zero. `absentVerified` sitting in this job's self-report at 0 would have looked like an instrument while being structurally incapable of firing; deleting it makes the absence of the state visible in the shape of the output, and the same reasoning made the emit sweep the right test.

Do not try to hand-copy a 'frozen pre-change fixture' as evidence of byte-identity. Two hand copies of the same object prove the copying was careful, not that the branch is unchanged. Run the branch AT the start commit in a detached worktree (git worktree add <dir> <sha> plus a node_modules junction), capture the real output, hash it, and assert the hash.

So the false-absence population's composition is settled arithmetic on a measured artifact, not an estimate -- only the live store's per-rail result remains unmeasured.

Whether a missing per-parcel BDC row is an acquisition need or a mapping gap is P-258's call, and it is now visible as unaccounted rather than hidden as a verified absence.

A write gate that only moves cells in one prior state freezes every cell a bad writer already stamped -- so a defect measured on ALREADY-WRITTEN data cannot be closed by fixing the writer alone. Check the gate's admitted prior states against the population the census measured before calling a writer fix a fix; if the measured cells are all in an earned state, the row is a gate row too.

Before releasing a cell by matching a provenance string, grep for EVERY writer of that string: the no-table finding this job releases is also written by parcel-envelope-cells.mjs. A release scoped by a batch's rail allowlist then rests on another module's rail list, so assert the disjointness against that module's own exported constant. 'The other job doesn't write my rails' is true until it isn't, and nothing fails when it stops being true.

A rebase that applies cleanly can still leave a stale invariant: after P-284 and P-256 both landed textually in one file, a comment stated the gate was 'unaccounted-only' while the code said otherwise. Read the other lane's prose in the merged file, not just the conflict markers -- the semantic merge is the reviewer's job, and git reports success either way.

Do not force-push a rebased branch and then try to make the push-triggered check green by re-running it: the workflow's BASE_REF is github.event.before, which still points at the now-unreachable pre-rebase tip. The only thing that clears it is a following push whose before-sha is reachable (a plain fast-forward), which is what cleared it here.

Fix .github/workflows/ci.yml:93-101 so the push leg of ldt-sha-comment-presence degrades gracefully when github.event.before is unfetchable (it already does this for the null-SHA first-push case): a force-pushed branch currently errors the check with exit 2 instead of skipping, producing a red check that says nothing about the diff. Owner: whoever owns the workflow file; this lane's scope is two files.
